content.text:
I've submitted index 10 (Sb fraction 0.26) as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.00058%, which is effectively zero, so the pick is essentially arbitrary: none of the measured compositions showed real photoactivity.

I used all 5 EQE measurements, spread across the line:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.12 | -0.00092 |
| 10 | 0.26 | 0.00058 |
| 14 | 0.39 | 0.00017 |
| 20 | 0.61 | -0.00025 |
| 28 | 0.82 | -0.00083 |

The last pick, index 14, came from the Gaussian-process tool's suggestion. After the first four results it predicted nothing above about 0.0004% anywhere on the line.

**Likely reason:** the illumination is 2.1 eV photons. The known Mg–Sb–O phases, from MgO through the Mg antimonates, are expected to have band gaps too wide to absorb much light at that energy. I didn't check this with the band-gap model, though.

**Not done:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements and ran no band-gap or stability calculations. So the phases in these films weren't identified.

**Not tested:** the unmeasured stretches, especially Sb 0.08–0.10 and 0.64–0.80, weren't tested directly. The flat results elsewhere make a strong performer there unlikely, but it can't be ruled out.
